title: Zoledronic acid · adjuvant breast treatment
context_label: Adjuvant breast cancer · postmenopausal (natural or treatment-induced)
schedule_summary: Zoledronic acid by IV infusion once every six months for up to five years, unless progression or unacceptable toxicity changes the plan. The usual source dose is 4 mg, with renal review before prescribing.
purpose: Reduce recurrence risk as part of the agreed early-breast treatment plan.
indication_text: Adjuvant breast cancer · postmenopausal (natural or treatment-induced)
administration_text: The infusion itself runs over at least 15 minutes. Preparation, blood review and observation make the visit longer. A port or take-home infusion pump is not routinely required for this medicine alone.
monitoring_summary: Before starting: renal profile, magnesium, calcium and phosphate. Check creatinine before every infusion; compare it with baseline as well as reviewing creatinine clearance. Correct low calcium and review vitamin D. Complete a dental assessment and preventive care before treatment where appropriate. Report dental symptoms; discuss invasive dental work with oncology and dental teams. Hydration is individualised, especially with heart failure.
review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

agents.name: Zoledronic acid
agents.explanation: Zoledronic acid binds to bone and reduces the activity of cells that break bone down. In selected people with early breast cancer it forms part of the adjuvant plan. It does not replace surgery, radiotherapy, chemotherapy or endocrine treatment.
agents.watch: Report jaw pain or a wound that will not heal, reduced urine, muscle cramps, eye pain or new thigh/groin pain.
risks: Flu-like reaction and muscle or joint pain
Rare atypical thigh fracture or eye inflammation

sections.title: Before an infusion
sections.text: Blood results, dental issues, supplements and current medicines are reviewed. The clinic confirms whether treatment can proceed.

sections.title: In the unit
sections.text: A peripheral cannula is often sufficient. The infusion is at least 15 minutes; ask about the full visit length.

sections.title: Between infusions
sections.text: Continue the prescribed supplements and dental care. Six-month spacing does not mean new symptoms should wait until the next visit.

sections.title: Planning completion
sections.text: The source allows up to five years. Confirm the individual duration and continuing endocrine/bone-health plan.

evidence.title: Why this treatment may be chosen
evidence.intro: This may be added to an adjuvant plan after discussing recurrence risk, menopause status, kidney function, dental health and the expected benefit. It is a separate treatment from medicines used to control bone metastases.
evidence.population: Adjuvant breast cancer · postmenopausal (natural or treatment-induced)
evidence.interpretation: Discuss how this evidence and the available alternatives apply to your own situation.
evidence.limitations: Discuss your own expected benefit, alternatives and uncertainty with the treating team.

teachback: Which medicines and doses are prescribed, when are they due, which checks are needed, and what would make you call the team today?
consent_support: Discuss the adjuvant off-label indication, renal risk, hypocalcaemia, jaw osteonecrosis, rare atypical fracture and alternatives. Record menopause status and the agreed duration.

support.title: Calcium and vitamin D
support.text: Follow the prescribed daily supplements; the team checks calcium and adjusts them if it is high or low.

support.title: Dental care
support.text: Keep routine dental care and tell the dentist about treatment. Report jaw pain or a wound that does not heal.

support.title: Flu-like symptoms
support.text: Aches or fever can occur after infusion. Use the agreed symptom plan; seek advice if severe or persistent.

support.title: Hydration
support.text: Follow the team’s fluid advice; heart or kidney problems may change it.

items.title: Your exact schedule
items.text: Zoledronic acid by IV infusion once every six months for up to five years, unless progression or unacceptable toxicity changes the plan. The usual source dose is 4 mg, with renal review before prescribing.

items.title: Alternatives
items.text: Discuss biomarker-directed, endocrine, chemotherapy and supportive-care options appropriate to this setting, including the option not to proceed.

chapters.title: Checks across treatment
chapters.intro: Your team arranges tests and reviews the results before treatment decisions.

items.title: Blood and organ checks
items.text: Before starting: renal profile, magnesium, calcium and phosphate. Check creatinine before every infusion; compare it with baseline as well as reviewing creatinine clearance. Correct low calcium and review vitamin D.

items.title: Other treatment-specific checks
items.text: Complete a dental assessment and preventive care before treatment where appropriate. Report dental symptoms; discuss invasive dental work with oncology and dental teams. Hydration is individualised, especially with heart failure.

items.title: Cancer review and follow-up
items.text: After early-breast treatment, breast imaging and clinical review follow the agreed plan. Routine CT/PET scans or blood tumour markers are not used to search for distant recurrence in someone without symptoms or clinical concerns.

items.title: Bone health
items.text: Bone-health assessment follows endocrine therapy, ovarian suppression, menopause and other fracture risks. It has its own monitoring plan.

chapters.title: The wider treatment plan
chapters.intro: Agree surgery, radiotherapy and endocrine treatment as applicable; their schedules and checks remain separate.

items.title: Treatment changes
items.text: A delayed, omitted or changed dose needs an updated plan from the treating team. Do not move doses or restart on your own.

items.title: Medicines review
items.text: Check new prescriptions, over-the-counter medicines and supplements with the oncology pharmacist before taking them.

items.title: After treatment
items.text: Keep the agreed follow-up and report persistent or new symptoms between visits.
